extracted.intended_audience: PAIMI grantees; Protection & Advocacy (P&A) systems; SAMHSA program staff; public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Revisions and instructions for the Protection and Advocacy for Individuals With Mental Illness (PAIMI) Annual Program Performance Report (PPR), PPR Instructions, and ACR, including new data categories, definitions, response coding rules, performance measures, budget/reporting tables, and items for public comment under the Paperwork Reduction Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment topics (Paperwork Reduction Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are invited on: (a) whether the proposed collections of information are necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information shall have practical utility; (b) the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information; (c) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (d) ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on respondents, including leveraging automated data collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should address one or more of the four specified PRA topics when submitting comments; the agency will use comments to evaluate necessity, burden estimates, clarity/utility, and burdensaving opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race question additions
rubrics_metrics.description: All questions related to Race; added the following choices of Some other race and Race unknown;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate the additional response categories into race-related fields in the PPR to capture respondents who do not identify with existing categories or whose race is unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender question additions
rubrics_metrics.description: All questions related to Gender; added the following choices of Transgender (Trans Woman and Trans Man), Two-Spirit for American Indian/Alaska Native (AIAN), Gender Non-Conforming, Other, and Prefer not to say;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the expanded gender response options in demographic fields and allow respondents to select 'Prefer not to say' where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual orientation question additions
rubrics_metrics.description: All questions related Sexual Orientation; added the following choices of Lesbian or gay, Straight (not lesbian or gay), Bisexual, Other, and Prefer not to say;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update sexual orientation tables/fields to present these choices; include 'Prefer not to say' as an explicit opt-out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic composition definitions and clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographic Composition of PAIMI Governing Board, Advisory Council and Program Staff; the following was added for clarification, 'Transgender is someone whose gender identity is incongruent with their sex assigned at birth. A trans woman or a transgender woman is a woman who was assigned male at birth. A trans man or a transgender man is a man who was assigned female at birth. Two-Spirit is a term by and for Indigenous peoples and is culturally anchored with a particular meaning and, potentially, social status, it is not appropriate for use by non-Indigenous populations. Gender Non-Conforming refers to people who do not follow other people's ideas or stereotypes about how they should look, or act based on the female or male sex they were assigned at birth. Lesbian is a woman who has a romantic and/or sexual orientation toward women. Gay is a man who has a romantic and/or sexual orientation toward men. Straight (not lesbian or gay) is a heterosexual person; someone having a romantic and/or sexual orientation to persons of the opposite sex. Bisexual is an individual who has the capacity to form enduring physical, romantic, and/or emotional attractions to those of the same gender or to those of another gender. Other is someone who does not identified exclusively in one of the categories for gender or sexual orientation and is identified with a different term.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided definitions in PPR Instructions when coding and reporting demographic composition for governing boards, advisory councils, and staff; note cultural specificity (e.g., Two-Spirit) and guidance about appropriateness of terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of mental health professionals on Advisory Council — 'Other' option
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of Mental Health Professionals on the Advisory Council; the following was added for clarification, Other (Identify the professional in the Footnotes);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'Other' is selected, specify the professional type in the footnotes to the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age question: 'Prefer not to say' clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: All questions related to Age; added the clarification 'would not disclose' to 'Prefer not to say';
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'Prefer not to say' as meaning the respondent 'would not disclose' age; ensure consistent coding/interpretation across age fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender and sexual orientation counts must be unduplicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender and Sexual Orientation of PAIMI-eligible Individuals Served; the following was added for clarification, 'Enter the number of individuals served by the indicated categories of gender and sexual orientation. Individuals should not be included in more than one of the categories. The total for both tables should be an unduplicated total of persons served based on gender and sexual orientation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filling tables, ensure individuals are assigned to only one category and totals are unduplicated across gender and sexual orientation tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living arrangements definitions and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Living Arrangements Section, the following definitions were added in the PPR Instructions for clarification: Community residential home for children/youth up to 18 yrs.; Community residential home for adults; Non-medical community-based residential facility for children/youth; Foster care; Nursing homes, including skilled nursing facilities; Intermediate care facilities (ICF); Public and Private general hospital involving emergency rooms; Public institutional living arrangement; Private institutional living arrangement; Psychiatric hospitals (public/private); Jails; State prisons; Federal detention centers; Federal prisons; Veterans' Administration hospital/clinic; Other Federal facility; Homeless; Independent (in the community & PAIMI-eligible); Parental or other family home & PAIMI-eligible; Unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PPR Instructions' definitions to classify living arrangements consistently; examples and distinctions (e.g., levels of care, public vs. private, juvenile vs. adult settings) are provided to guide coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints/Problems dispositions added
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Complaints/Problems of PAIMI-eligible Individuals of Abuse, Neglect, and Rights Violations Section, the following dispositions were added; e. Other indicators of success or outcomes that resulted from P&A involvement. h. P&A withdrew due to conflict of interest or other reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these additional disposition codes when documenting complaint/problem outcomes and reasons for case closure; provide explanatory footnotes where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas of Alleged Rights Violations — new choices
rubrics_metrics.description: In Areas of Alleged Rights Violations Section, the following choices were added for clarification; w. The denial of access to personal possessions x. Failure to comply with commitment regulations y. Failure to comply with commitment time frames
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the new codes to capture these specific categories of alleged rights violations in reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention Strategies — Abuse/Neglect Investigation code
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice A/N I—Abuse/Neglect Investigation was added to the Intervention Strategies for clarification;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record 'A/N I' when the intervention strategy involved an abuse/neglect investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for closing individual advocacy case file — expanded dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Reasons for Closing Individual Advocacy Case File Section, the following choices were either reorganized or added for clarification; Client's objective was partially or fully met. Case or investigation lacked merit. Case withdrawn or terminated by the client. Issue favorably resolved. Issue not favorably resolved. Other success or outcomes due to P&A involvement (i.e., provided self-advocacy assistance) Other representation found. Services not needed due to client's death or relocation. P&A withdrew due to conflict of interest or other reasons (i.e., client would not cooperate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the clarified/expanded reason codes to categorize case closures; include contextual notes or footnotes when selecting 'Other' or to explain withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death investigation reporting clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Death Investigation Activities Section, the following was added for clarification, 'if zero means the P&A did not receive any death reports from CMS for investigation, please note this in the Footnotes';
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If zero deaths are reported because no reports were received, explicitly state that in the footnotes rather than leaving ambiguous zeros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Advocacy label correction
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Interventions on behalf of groups of PAIMI-eligible Individuals Section, Group Advocacy the term 'non-litigation' was corrected;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the 'Group Advocacy' intervention type is labeled correctly (non-litigation) in tables and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: access to community-based services and community integration
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who access community-based mental health or health care services that resulted in community integration and independence or are better able to advocate to do so;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts/outcomes for individuals who accessed community-based services that led to integration/independence or improved advocacy capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: access to benefits or services
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who access benefits or services or are better able to advocate to do so;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report individuals who secured benefits/services or improved ability to advocate for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: improved living settings
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who live in a healthier, safer, improved, or more integrated settings or are better able to advocate to do so;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report cases where living conditions improved or individuals gained advocacy capacity to achieve such settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: remain in own home
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals are able to stay in their own home or better able to advocate to do so;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document instances where P&A involvement helped individuals remain in their homes or improved their advocacy ability to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: employment and workplace protections
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who can secure or maintain employment and/or are not subject to workplace discrimination or are better able to advocate for to do so;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report successful employment outcomes or improved protection against workplace discrimination attributable to P&A activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: appropriate educational services and supports
rubrics_metrics.description: (f) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who receive appropriate educational services and supports and/or are not subject to discrimination in educational settings or are better able to advocate for those outcomes;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count individuals who obtained appropriate educational services/supports or improved advocacy for such outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: safer school conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: (g) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who go to school in safe and more humane conditions;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report changes leading to safer/humane school conditions for PAIMI-eligible children/youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: integrated services for children
rubrics_metrics.description: (h) 'PAIMI-eligible children (individuals) who receive appropriate services in the most integrated settings;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document children receiving services in the least restrictive, most integrated settings appropriate to their needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: non-discrimination in government benefits/services/housing/public accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who were not subject to discrimination in government benefits/services, housing, public accommodations, etc. or are better able to advocate for such outcomes;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record instances where discrimination was prevented/rectified or where advocacy capacity improved to prevent such discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: absence of abuse, neglect, or rights violations
rubrics_metrics.description: (j) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who were not subject to abuse, neglect, or rights violations or are better able to advocate for to do so;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report outcomes showing prevention/cessation of abuse/neglect/rights violations or improved self-advocacy to prevent them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: decision-making capacity/choice
rubrics_metrics.description: (k) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who can make their own decisions to the maximum extent feasible or are better able to advocate to do so;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document increased autonomy or improved advocacy enabling decision-making by individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: rights enforcement/restoration/expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: (l) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who had their rights enforced, retained, restored and/or expanded or are better able to advocate for to do so;'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count cases where rights were enforced/restored/expanded or individuals improved advocacy for rights-related outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measure: voting participation
rubrics_metrics.description: (m) 'PAIMI-eligible individuals who were more able to participate in the voting process or are better able to advocate for to do so.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report activities/outcomes that increased voter participation or advocacy capacity related to voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget section: tables and instructions added
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and instructions were added the Budget Section for clarification;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the newly added budget tables and follow updated instructions when reporting budgetary information in the PPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Priorities (Goals) reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Statement of Priorities (Goals) Section, removed the words 'Expected Target' and revised the following information for clarification: Report on Previous FY Statement of Priorities and Objectives (SPO). The Priority and Objectives target population and expected outcome fields will be pre-populated by the information submitted with the PAIMI application. The number of pre-populated items will reflect the number submitted in the application. A. Please indicate an actual outcome for each expected outcome. B. Please indicate strategies to implement goals and priorities. C. Provide a narrative (500-word limit) of P&A activities for each of the accomplishments related to each priority. D. Other Qualitative Narrative related to each priority: Provide a narrative (500 words limit) of significant activity for which there were no quantifiable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each pre-populated priority/objective, report the actual outcome, describe strategies used, submit a 500-word narrative of related P&A activities, and provide a separate 500-word qualitative narrative for significant but non-quantifiable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date for revised report formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The current report formats will be effective for the FY 2023 PPR reports due on January 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P&A systems should use the revised formats/instructions for reports due Jan 1, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated annualized hour burden (PPR and ACR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of Annualized Hour Burden: Program Performance Report — respondents 57, responses per respondent 1, hours per response 20, total hour burden 1,140. Advisory Council Report — respondents 57, responses per respondent 1, hours per response 10, total hour burden 570. Total respondents 114; total hour burden 1,710. *Based on past estimates and the fact that changes being made do not measurably impact response burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice provides these burden estimates and states the changes do not measurably impact response burden; commenters may address accuracy of these estimates under PRA comment topics.
